title: Regional partition + GPU backpressure stress-injector and circuit-breaker validation
creator: Maya Alvarez
description:
Goal: Build and run a deterministic stress-injection harness that simulates a regional network partition while progressively exhausting GPU pool capacity in the primary region to validate our circuit-breaker and load-shedding policies and multi-region failover behavior. The test should prove graceful degradation and safe failover without cascading control-plane failures and should surface observable signals that map to SLO consumption.

Scope:
- Simulate a partial region isolation (egress limited, degraded inter-region links) that increases request latency and drops control-plane heartbeats.
- Inject GPU pool backpressure by spawning allocation-heavy synthetic workloads that saturate GPU memory/KV cache and produce per-pool queue growth.
- Emulate dependency blackholes for a subset of external services (metrics ingestion, model store, auth) to validate timeouts and fallback paths.
- Validate circuit-breakers (per-route and per-customer) trip within configured thresholds and that automatic shedding preserves high-priority traffic.
- Verify automatic multi-region failover routes traffic to secondary region within target window and that request contexts are honored.

Acceptance criteria (measurable):
1) Failover latency: 95% of affected requests routed to secondary region within 45s of partition start.
2) SLO preservation: For high-priority routes, p95 latency increase <= 2x baseline and error rate increase <= 2x baseline during steady-state of the experiment. Total SLO burn for the run must be < 3% of the scenario budget.
3) Circuit-breaker correctness: breakers must open and prevent >90% of queued requests from reaching overloaded GPU pools (verify via pool.queue_size and serve.rejected_by_cb metrics).
4) No control-plane cascade: control-plane errors should remain <1% across the fleet; auto-scaling decisions must not oscillate.
5) Observability: dashboards must show clear signals (per-region throughput, per-pool queue latency, KV cache miss amplification) and the run must produce a postmortem with root cause and recommended mitigations.

Test plan and phases:
A) Harness development (unit + integration): implement 'stress-injector' binary (k8s job + canary traffic generator) that can: throttle egress to simulate partition, create synthetic GPU-saturating jobs, and flip dependency endpoints to blackhole. Add feature flags to constrain to test namespaces.
B) Dry run in staging: run with 10% of traffic, collect telemetry, validate safe stop hooks.
C) Canary in non-critical region: run with 25% of relevant tenant traffic and monitor for control-plane regressions.
D) Controlled production validation (optional, gated by SRE): run targeted against test tenant(s) with rapid rollback window; abort on any breach of rollback criteria below.

Rollback criteria (abort experiment immediately):
- Control-plane error rate > 1.5% for >5 minutes.
- Any customer reports of data loss or incorrect inference outputs.
- Automated watchdog indicates CPU/GPU thermal events or node eviction rising >2x baseline.

Runbook highlights:
- Preflight checklist: confirm circuit-breaker thresholds, canary routing policies, alerting hooks and paging config.
- Abort steps: disable stress-injector job, flip routing to allow gradual reintroduction, scale up dedicated pools if necessary, and open an incident with SRE.

Observability & telemetry to capture:
- Per-region: request rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate, route-fallback counts.
- Per-GPU-pool: allocation attempts, queue_size, avg_queue_latency, kv_cache_hit_ratio, eviction_rate.
- Control plane: heartbeat misses, coordinator errors, autoscaler decision latency.
- Downstream dependencies: auth latencies/timeouts, model-store errors.

Artifacts and links:
- Design doc (confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RES/Regional+Stress+Injector+Design
- Harness repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/resilience-stress-injector (PRs below)
- Safety dashboard (Datadog): https://app.datadoghq.com/dashboard/redwood/resilience-stress-safety

Notes on scope exclusions: we will not perform global region cutover nor test on production-critical customers without Director-level approval. The initial runs are limited to test tenants and canary traffic only.
comments: 2026-02-22 - Kickoff: scoped test matrix and identified metrics owners (SRE: Priya Chandra, Runtime: Luis Moreno). Maya created initial design doc and set up Confluence page.

2026-02-25 - PR #212 merged to add the stress-injector k8s job and adjustable backpressure knobs. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/resilience-stress-injector/pull/212. Unit tests + basic integration tests added.

2026-03-01 - Dry run in staging: injected slow egress to eu-west and spun synthetic GPU workloads. Observed KV cache miss amplification in pool-3 leading to p95 spikes. Added instrumentation: pool.kv_cache_hit_ratio metric (PR #218).

2026-03-03 - Investigation: KV cache thrash traced to synthetic workload creating many short-lived key prefixes. Short-term mitigation: increase local cache TTL for test runs and cap per-job prefix churn. Filed follow-up ENG ticket ENG-30902 to harden cache accessor fallback behavior.

2026-03-05 - Circuit-breaker adjust: initial configuration tripped too late under slow-start workloads. Tuned thresholds to be more sensitive to queue growth and added hysteresis to avoid flapping (PR #226). Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/226

2026-03-07 - Canary run in non-critical region: 25% test-traffic. Result: breakers opened as expected, failover to secondary region completed with median failover time ~28s. However, control-plane coordinator CPU spiked by 40% for 3 minutes due to alert floods — added rate limit to alerting pipeline.

2026-03-09 - Post-canary analysis: SLO burn stayed within acceptable bounds for high-priority routes (~1.7%). Action items: add a per-tenant priority tag to stress-injector so we can selectively exercise lower-priority workloads during next run.

2026-03-10 - Next steps: prepare gated production run checklist, schedule SRE war room, and implement the per-tenant priority filter. Assigned follow-up: Noah to land tenant-filter PR and coordinate calendar with SRE for 2026-03-16 window.
